review_notes: I read the whole target file and checked the related definitions and the other files that repeat its auxiliary lemmas. The file declares no simp attributes of its own. The line-8 `attribute [-simp]` removes only restricted-product and Borel lemmas, and I found no evidence it affects the `diagUnits2` reasoning. The main `solution` proof uses `simp` only trivially. I found no loop or competing-rule problem. The findings are about missing simp or rewrite lemmas around `diagUnits2`, `torusEquiv`, and `glArch ∘ centralScalar`, which push the proofs into fallback `simp` chains and explicit unfolding. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim that any proposed replacement compiles. For the `gamma_entries` suggestion I did not confirm the exact shape of `glArch_centralScalar_mul_diagUnits2`; I inferred it from its use at the `hγ'` step of `solution`.

findings.problem: `coe_diagUnits2` is a simp lemma for the forward matrix of `diagUnits2 x y`. There is no simp lemma for the matrix of its inverse, `((diagUnits2 x y)⁻¹ : Matrix …)`. The inverse half of the proof therefore has to unfold the definition with `simp [diagUnits2]`. Both halves hedge with a five-way `first | simpa … | (have … simp at …) | …` chain, which suggests the author could not predict the simp normal form of the entries. The `first` alternatives are brittle: if one `simp` call changes behaviour, a different branch runs silently. The fallback branches are redundant noise.
findings.proposed_change: In Definitions/Def_LanglandsTunnell_CubicInduction_TorusValues.lean, next to `coe_diagUnits2`, add an `rfl` lemma stating `((diagUnits2 x y)⁻¹ : GL (Fin 2) A) : Matrix …) = !![((x⁻¹ : Aˣ) : A), 0; 0, ((y⁻¹ : Aˣ) : A)]`, tagged `@[simp]`. Check that it does not conflict with existing `Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val` style rules, since the coercion of `Units.inv` through `GL` is delicate. Then replace each `first` block with a single `simpa using Units.continuous_val.comp continuous_fst` (or its `coe_inv` analogue), with no `[diagUnits2]` unfolding.
findings.benefit: The proof becomes deterministic and short, and the `diagUnits2` definition stays closed. Every other file that currently needs `simp [diagUnits2]` for inverse entries gets the same normal form.

findings.problem: `torusEquiv` is a bundled `≃ₜ*` defined by a `where` block. The only lemma that computes it, `torusEquiv_apply`, is not `@[simp]`, and it is proved by unfolding the definition. Nothing computes `(torusEquiv …).symm`. Downstream code that has `e z p` for `e z := PccTorus.torusEquiv …` (in `solution`, and in the `ρ.prod ρ).map (e z)` integrals) cannot reduce it without unfolding the definition. This file already needs a separate `integral_map_torusEquiv` plus a `rfl` coercion detour to get at the underlying `diagUnits2` expression.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `torusEquiv_apply` `@[simp]`. Its LHS is the coercion of a bundled-equiv application, and its RHS is the canonical `diagUnits2` form that `coe_diagUnits2` then expands. This is the standard shape for such lemmas and cannot loop. Add a companion lemma for `(torusEquiv …).symm t` giving `(unit00 …, unit11 …)`, or its coordinates, so both directions have simp-normal forms.
findings.benefit: Users of `torusEquiv`, including the copies of this construction in the sibling files, can use plain `simp` and no longer need `simp [torusEquiv]` or `show … from rfl` bridges.

findings.problem: The rewriting of `glArch (centralScalar z * diagUnits2 a b)` is done by an ad hoc `simp only` set. It combines a local, non-simp `rfl` entry lemma (`glArch_apply`), which shadows the differently stated `AdelicLevel.glArch_apply` in Definitions. It also uses a non-simp lemma `val_centralScalar_mul_diagUnits2` that gives a `!![…]` literal, plus a long list of `Matrix.cons_val*` and `of_apply` lemmas that spell out the matrix-literal normal form. The simp interface has no canonical form for 'glArch of scalar times diagonal'. The proof is therefore tied to the shape of the `!![ ]` literal simp set. Two of the three entries are then finished by `rw` chains (line 209) rather than simp. A lemma for the whole product already exists in Theorems: `AutomorphicForm.glArch_centralScalar_mul_diagUnits2`, which `solution` uses at `hγ'`.
findings.proposed_change: Reduce `glArch (centralScalar z * diagUnits2 a b)` with the existing lemma `AutomorphicForm.glArch_centralScalar_mul_diagUnits2` (giving `scalar (Fin 2) (adeleArch z) * diagUnits2 …`), then finish with `coe_diagUnits2` and the `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.scalar` coercion lemmas. Alternatively, state entry lemmas `(0,0)`, `(1,1)`, `(0,1)`, `(1,0)` for `val_centralScalar_mul_diagUnits2` and mark them `@[simp]`, so the goals in `gamma_entries` close with one `simp`. Remove the redundant local `glArch_apply`, or fold it into the Definitions lemma by stating it with `.1`.
findings.benefit: The proof no longer depends on the `Matrix.cons_val*` lemma set. The three conjuncts can be proved uniformly. The lemma `gamma_entries` is likely to survive small simp-set changes better.
